\section[bāyārike]{\kn{ಬಾಯಾರಿಕೆ} (bāyārike) — thirst}

\label{lesson:KA-C84-thirst}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for anger, then the Kannada for laughter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬಾಯಾರಿಕೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಾಯಾರಿಕೆ}} (\emph{bāyārike}) — \textquotedblleft{}thirst\textquotedblright{}. It begins with \textbf{\kn{ಬಾಯಿ}} (\emph{bāyi}), \textquotedblleft{}mouth\textquotedblright{}, which you already know: thirst is a dry mouth.

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಬಾಯಾರಿಕೆ}} (\emph{nanage bāyārike}) — \textquotedblleft{}I am thirsty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Hunger's partner: the body asking for water.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāyārike}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāyārike}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage bāyārike}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for anger, then the Kannada for laughter, then say \emph{bāyārike} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬಾಯಾರಿಕೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thirst\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sustu]{\kn{ಸುಸ್ತು} (sustu) — weariness, feeling worn out}

\label{lesson:KA-C84-weariness}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for laughter, then the Kannada for thirst.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸುಸ್ತು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸುಸ್ತು}} (\emph{sustu}) — \textquotedblleft{}weariness\textquotedblright{}, the everyday word for feeling worn out.

\textbf{\kn{ಸುಸ್ತಾಗಿದೆ}} (\emph{sustāgide}) — \textquotedblleft{}I'm worn out\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ಆಯಾಸ}} is a little more formal; \textbf{\kn{ಸುಸ್ತು}} is what you hear at home.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The everyday cousin of āyāsa.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sustu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sustu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sustāgide}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for laughter, then the Kannada for thirst, then say \emph{sustu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಸುಸ್ತು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Weariness, feeling worn out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bevaru]{\kn{ಬೆವರು} (bevaru) — sweat}

\label{lesson:KA-C84-sweat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for thirst, then the Kannada for weariness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬೆವರು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬೆವರು}} (\emph{bevaru}) — \textquotedblleft{}sweat\textquotedblright{}, and also \textquotedblleft{}to sweat\textquotedblright{}.

On a hot day in the \textbf{\kn{ಬಿಸಿಲು}} (\emph{bisilu}), \textquotedblleft{}sunshine\textquotedblright{}, this is the word you need.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What the sunshine does to the body.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bevaru}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bevaru}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bevaru}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for thirst, then the Kannada for weariness, then say \emph{bevaru} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬೆವರು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sweat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āspatre]{\kn{ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ} (āspatre) — hospital}

\label{lesson:KA-C84-hospital}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for weariness, then the Kannada for sweat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ}} (\emph{āspatre}) — \textquotedblleft{}hospital\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ} \kn{ಎಲ್ಲಿ}?} (\emph{āspatre elli?}) — \textquotedblleft{}where is the hospital?\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ಎಲ್ಲಿ}}, \textquotedblleft{}where\textquotedblright{}, which you already know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A place to ask for when the body needs help.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āspatre}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āspatre}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{āspatre elli?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for weariness, then the Kannada for sweat, then say \emph{āspatre} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hospital\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
